prompt:
Use the attached clay render as the exact blueprint. Keep every wall, the corner, the window opening and its deep reveals, cornice, skirting, floor and ceiling lines, the camera height, lens and angle, and the position, size and angle of every furniture piece (sofa, coffee table, armchair) exactly as in the clay. Move, resize, add or remove nothing. Only turn the clay into real materials and real light, and add the products listed below at their stated places.

Photoreal editorial photograph for a top Scandinavian interiors magazine: a Copenhagen living room at 3 pm in mid-winter. 24 mm shift lens at 1.2 m, level, verticals straight, deep focus.

Light: the tall north window on the left is the only key light, a large soft source, no direct sun. Light falls off across the room: the back wall is brightest by the corner and a half stop darker at the right edge; the window wall sits in soft shade. Every object has a lit left face, a soft shadow side and a feathered shadow falling right and slightly toward the camera, with short contact shadows. The reveals glow; the window is the brightest area yet holds detail: a pale winter garden. White balance 4600 K: warm white walls, never pink, yellow or grey. Lamps on, low, 2700 K, shades glowing, no lamp shadows: warm pools on the sofa's right end (floor lamp), the armchair (reading lamp) and the table centre (pendant); soft fans up and down the wall (travertine). Real contrast, never milky.

Materials: matte warm-white mineral paint with a faint chalky movement in the raking light. Wide oiled white-oak planks, 25 cm by 3-4 m, pale honey, long straight grain, matte. Slubby oatmeal cotton-linen sofa on tapered oak legs; oiled light oak table and armchair frame; mist-grey wool boucle armchair cushions.

Products, exactly these:
1. Hero, above the sofa, centred at 1.48 m: three 50 x 70 cm portrait prints, minimal geometric shapes in oatmeal, sand and charcoal on warm off-white with a printed white border, in thin light-oak frames 6 cm apart, no glare.
2. Flanking them above each sofa end: two 8 x 16 cm honed travertine block wall lamps, hardwired.
3. Left wall between the window and the camera, over the armchair's back: a matte black folding swing-arm lamp with a tapered oatmeal linen shade, bulb hidden; a short straight cord into a flush socket just below.
4. Right of the sofa: an empty 38 cm seagrass belly basket, hiding the base of a floor lamp: a slim light natural-wood tripod with a tall warm-white fabric column shade, its top below the right travertine lamp.
5. A 230 x 330 cm flat braided wool rug, cream and oatmeal in soft tone-on-tone bands, no fringe, long side along the sofa, under its front legs and the table; the armchair's front legs on it.
6. Sheer natural linen-blend curtains, visible slub, S-fold, slim black rod under the cornice, open in narrow stacks beside the glass, backlit, hems on the floor.
7. Sill, back casement: a 31 cm cream distressed clay jar vase with three or four eucalyptus stems.
8. Back wall left of the sofa, low: a 30 cm round raffia sunburst.
9. High above the table centre: a closed 40 cm flattened pumpkin lantern in warm-white ribbed fabric on a thin black rod.
10. Sofa: warm-white boucle and sage knitted cushions at the left end, a charcoal linen lumbar at the right, a crinkled warm-white muslin throw over the right arm.
11. Table: a grey-sage linen runner with short fringe across the left third; bare oak centre; at the right two travertine pedestal holders with unlit pillar candles, the taller at left, and a 21 cm warm-white stoneware bowl in front, empty.

Nothing else: no plant, pouf, magazines, books, mirror, glass or loose cable. No text, no people. No sun patches, beams, bloom, haze, glow halos, HDR look, grain or vignette.
prompt_deviation: lines starting with # stripped as the file header instructs (3,771 chars sent of 5,861 in the file)

exposure.flag: DARK: needs more than +0.2 stop, not lifted further

grade.rule: docs/render-recipe-nordic-2026-10-24.md 2.6: WB on the hero-wall patch, exposure capped +-0.2 stop, chroma -10%, roll-off from L 94, S curve 0.12, black point to L 12.5 only if below 12, no grain, no vignette

clay_lock.method: phase correlation of gradient maps vs the clay resized to the output, per region (du/dv as frame fractions); peaks below ~0.03 are unreliable, so the verdict is visual (clay-edge overlay) with the numbers as support

self_check_verdict: Clay lock holds on walls, window, sofa, armchair and the original table (auto worst 0.014), but the model ADDED a second coffee table in the foreground and rendered NONE of the 11 products (no prints, lamps, curtains, rug, vase, cushions, runner); grey sofa, rough plaster, a sun patch on the back wall, very dark (needs +2.3 stop). Not retaken: the lock itself held; a retake (480) needs the manager's word.
